transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-16 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Derek (Redwood SE), Anya (Redwood CSM) - Liam (CTO), Priya (Head of ML), Carlos (FinOps), Jenna (SRE)

00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro round?
00:06 Liam: Hi I'm Liam, CTO at Siren. we run a recommendation feed and want to add an LLM assistant across agents. Trying to understand cost impact.
00:12 Priya: Priya, Head of ML, i'll be driving evaluation and accuracy tradeoffs.
00:17 Carlos: Carlos on FinOps, i'll own budget gating.
00:20 Maya: Awesome. Derek, do you want to kick off with how Redwood thinks about per-token economics?
00:25 Derek: Sure. So high-level we break unit cost into model-variant price + infra efficiency. For hosted we publish per-token rates for each model tier, and then there are levers—batching, kv cache, quantization—that reduce effective per-token cost. Example: for a 4k context gpt-like open model you might see base hosted at X cents per 1k tokens but with caching and batching that effective rate falls by 30-60% depending on hit rate.
00:45 Priya: Sorry can you repeat the caching bit, what do you mean by kv cache hit rate?
00:49 Derek: Sure. If you have repeated prefixes or multi-turn chat we keep KV cache across tokens so we don't recompute earlier key/values. If you have 70% reuse of context the per-token work is much lower. I might say KV sometimes spoken as K V cash in transcripts, so apologies for any transcript noise.
01:05 Carlos: That sounds promising but our CFO wants a hard ceiling: 200k USD/mo for inference. We need to know which hosting mode gets us closest while hitting 95th percentile latency under 250ms for short queries.
01:18 Maya: Good constraint. Can you share expected QPS and typical prompt lengths?
01:21 Priya: For the assistant feature, average prompt 120 tokens input, 180 tokens output. Peak QPS about 30 requests/sec, sustained 12 QPS. We also have batch offline re-ranking jobs at night.
01:36 Derek: With that profile, two levers stand out: batching for high throughput tasks (re-ranking) and KV caching for the assistant flow. If your assistant is multi-turn, cache hit could be high. For the 12 sustained QPS, hosted is likely easiest to start; Dedicated is where you buy reserved GPU pools so you get lower per-token if you commit.
01:55 Jenna: On Private, our security team will want VPC peering and KMS integration, plus audit logs. How much of a lift is that?
02:04 Derek: We support Private with customer-controlled VPC and KMS/HSM. Integration is non-trivial — network setup, routing, and potentially opening up bastion or private link. Typical timeline 6-10 weeks for a first pass depending on network approvals.
02:20 Liam: Timeline matters - product deadline in 10 weeks. So Private may be tight.
02:25 Maya: Right. So immediate path could be Hosted pilot to prove UX and cost, then Dedicated or Private later. Carlos, for budget math: do you want best-case and worst-case scenarios?
02:37 Carlos: Yes. Also want sensitivity to cache hit rate and batch size. We don't want surprises if usage scales.
02:44 Derek: We'll run two sensitivity slices: (1) assistant path (focus on KV hit) and (2) batch rerank (focus on throughput and batching). We'll show per-token and per-request costs across hit rates 0, 30, 60, 80% and batch sizes 1, 8, 32.
03:02 Priya: One question - quantization. How much accuracy hit do you see on open models when moving to int8/4-bit?
03:09 Derek: Varies by model. For many generation tasks int8 is near transparent; int4 can show some drop depending on model and prompt. We recommend doing side-by-side evals on your prompt set. Redwood Optimize will suggest quant and batching profiles per workload.
03:24 Carlos: Any hidden charges in Hosted? Network egress? Storage of KV?
03:29 Maya: Hosted pricing is mostly per-token and embedding units; there are also optional retention/long-term storage add-ons and egress is standard cloud egress we can itemize. We try to be transparent in the worksheet.
03:40 Liam: For Dedicated, how do you handle burst? If we buy committed capacity but have spikes at 100 QPS, will we throttle?
03:48 Derek: Dedicated can be configured with burst pools and autoscaling policies. You set a baseline reserved commit and configure burst to tap into shared capacity if available; pricing for burst is different. We'll show a model with reserved baseline plus a burst buffer cost.
04:02 Priya: ok practical ask — can we run a 2-day benchmark to validate latency at 95th perc and get an empirical per-token burn?
04:09 Derek: Absolutely. We'll provide a runner script and config to replay sample traces. We'll need access to sample request traces and preferred region.
04:18 Maya: Next steps then: we'll send the cost worksheet, SOC2 docs and Private deployment diagram. We'll schedule benchmark session — propose Tuesday next week 14:00 UTC.
04:30 Carlos: That works. Also can you include a mid-point scenario where we start Hosted but reserve Dedicated after X months? CFO wants runway options.
04:39 Maya: Yes, we'll include Hosted->Dedicated migration path with cost inflection points.
04:44 Priya: A minor clarification on latency targets — 95th under 250ms for the assistant when using caching, but for re-rank nightly batch we care about throughput not p95.
04:56 Derek: Noted. We'll tailor the benchmark scripts accordingly.
05:03 Liam: One more thing: data residency. Some of our users are EU-based; will we be able to pin region?
05:09 Maya: Yes Hosted supports region pinning for deployments; Private obviously you control residency. Dedicated we can provision in region but it's part of enterprise onboarding.
05:19 Jenna: Also need RBAC and SSO for team access.
05:23 Maya: We have SAML SSO and role-based access, plus audit logs available for Dedicated/Private. We'll attach a short security checklist.
05:33 Carlos: Good. Are there any competitors who do this cheaper?
05:36 Derek: There's always a tradeoff. Large providers may have volume discounts; self-hosted Triton setups can be cheaper but require ops. We'll include a competitor notes section.
05:46 Maya: Okay let's recap and assign owners.
05:50 Liam: Thanks all.

Transcript notes: occasional transcription artifacts (model names, KV spelled K V), filler words, and overlapping talk.

End of call.
